source: Light travels in straight lines. When something blocks it, a shadow forms on the other side. The closer the object is to the light, the bigger its shadow.
Thinking shadows are made of something or are a reflection. A shadow is just the place the light cannot reach.
Stand in the sun and a dark shape follows you: your shadow. Why is it there?
Light travels in straight lines. When something blocks it, the place behind it gets no light: a shadow. The closer the object is to the light, the bigger its shadow.
Slide the block toward the lamp and away. Watch the shadow on the wall grow and shrink.
Things that block light make shadows: we call them opaque, like wood or your hand. Transparent things, like clear glass, let light through. Translucent things, like wax paper, let some through.
Rays from the lamp spread out in straight lines. Close to the lamp, the block stops a wide fan of rays, so a big patch of wall goes dark.
You want a giant shadow puppet on the wall. Where do you hold your hand?
Close to the flashlight, far from the wall.
Shadows grow as the object gets closer to the light.
Thinking a shadow is a kind of reflection or is made of something. It is only the place the light cannot reach.
